International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

The day's developments are dominated by humanitarian and geopolitical crises across multiple continents. The WHO has warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is on pace to become the deadliest on record, with over 4,300 cases and 2,000 deaths since May [BBC]. In Colombia, rescuers are in the final hours of the critical 72-hour window to find survivors of Monday's magnitude 7.4 earthquake, which has killed at least 265 people [France 24, Globe and Mail]. The conflict between Russia and Ukraine continues to escalate, with Ukraine launching a major strike on Russia's Novorossiysk port that damaged grain terminals and reportedly hit four warships [BBC, France 24], while Russia retaliated by striking Ukraine's Izmail port [Al Jazeera]. President Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands, drawing a sharp protest from Japan [France 24]. In southern Africa, Zambia heads to the polls in a tight election testing President Hichilema's economic record amid cost-of-living concerns [RFI, Al Jazeera, France 24]. Meanwhile, Venezuela's interim government and opposition concluded their first round of talks with agreements on judicial reform and accessing frozen funds for earthquake recovery [France 24].

Top Stories
01 Health

Ebola Outbreak in DRC on Track to Become Deadliest Ever, WHO Warns

  • WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the 2026 outbreak will 'eclipse' the 2014-2016 epidemic that killed at least 11,000 people if current trends continue
  • The outbreak, declared May 15, has caused over 4,300 cases and more than 2,000 deaths; evidence suggests the virus began spreading in February but was initially misdiagnosed
  • The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or therapeutic drugs exist
  • WHO aims to bring transmission under control within three months but faces challenges from regional instability near the outbreak's center

02 Conflict

Ukraine Strikes Russia's Novorossiysk Port in 'Unique Operation,' Hitting Warships and Grain Terminals

  • Ukraine launched a combined drone and missile attack on Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea port and current home of most of Russia's Black Sea fleet
  • Three people including an eight-year-old child were killed and 24 injured; two major grain export terminals were damaged
  • Ukraine's military claimed four Russian warships including two frigates were hit; Russia has not confirmed naval losses
  • President Zelensky stated Ukraine needs 5-10% of US Patriot interceptor stockpiles to defend against Russian ballistic missiles

Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Reaches 265 as Rescue Efforts Enter Final Phase

  • The magnitude 7.4 earthquake, the strongest to hit Colombia this century, struck Monday and has killed at least 265 people with nearly 500 officially missing
  • Rescuers are approaching the critical 72-hour window for finding survivors; possible signs of life detected beneath collapsed bakery in Pereira
  • Over 3,500 people injured and more than 25,800 families affected across Cali, Pereira, Manizales, and Quibdo
  • Regional aid has begun arriving; a woman was rescued alive Tuesday after 36 hours trapped

04 Geopolitics

Zambia Votes in Close Election as Economic Hardship Tests Hichilema's Record

  • 8.7 million Zambians are voting in presidential, parliamentary, and local elections with polls open from 6am to 6pm local time
  • President Hakainde Hichilema seeks a second term running on economic reforms including debt restructuring and reduced inflation (now 6.8%)
  • Main challenger Brian Mundubile leads an opposition alliance backed by supporters of late former president Edgar Lungu
  • More than 70% of Zambia's 22 million people live on less than $3 a day; analysts describe the race as '50-50' due to cost-of-living frustrations

05 Geopolitics

Putin Visits Disputed Kuril Islands, Prompting Strong Japanese Protest

  • Russian President Vladimir Putin visited the Kuril Islands near Hokkaido for the first time, touring a fish-processing plant
  • Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi issued a 'strong protest,' stating the Northern Territories are 'an inherent part of Japan's territory'
  • The islands were seized by the Soviet Union in 1945; the territorial dispute has prevented a formal peace treaty between Russia and Japan
  • The visit came during Russian naval drills and a meeting on 'ensuring the security of Russia's eastern borders'
